setup.caveat: boundary-only labels from setup.exe cross-binary provenance; assuming setup.exe links the same library objects whole, a setup-identical function's same-CU sibling would also appear in setup.exe. Pairs in which either side is shorter than `wc1.modules_setup`'s identity minimum are excluded: that matcher cannot call such a function identical, so its status says nothing about object identity. No same-CU labels, so this corpus measures detection, not precision.

ground_truth_rule.exploratory: The war.exe game range is NEVER ground truth and is not part of any precision/recall number here.
ground_truth_rule.libsig: Corpus B1: a 10.0a clib3r.lib / cstrtx3r.obj object's contiguous _TEXT contribution; pairs are labelled only when both functions lie in matched extents and no non-padding bytes sit between them.
ground_truth_rule.setup: Corpus B2: setup.exe provenance; adjacent (identical, not identical) pairs are boundaries under the whole-object-link premise. Pairs in which either side is shorter than the setup identity matcher's minimum are excluded (it cannot call such a function identical). Boundary labels only, so precision is not measurable on this corpus.
ground_truth_rule.synthetic: Corpus A: CU membership from the build recipe, verified against the 10.0a wlink map; every adjacent function pair is labelled.

rubric.note: The rubric summarises measured precision only. `proven constraint` is not a metric label: it names a logical constraint whose premise is stated in the signal's `assumption` field, and the corpus reports how often the premise fails in practice.
